title: SlideCast Studio v4.1 “FRAME”
subtitle: Update — per-slide layout, active sticker motion and video export improvements
description: SlideCast Studio v4.1 FRAME adds per-slide image, character and subtitle layout, layout copying, active sticker motion, multilingual fonts, lighter backups and 30/60fps export.
author: aokuma
hero_alt: SlideCast Studio v4.1 FRAME — Make every slide clearer.
source_note: See the note article for later additions and comments.

blocks.title: 🌐 About the screenshots
blocks.text: The interface screenshots on this page use the Japanese edition. The English captions explain the relevant controls and behaviour.

blocks.html:
SlideCast Studio has been updated to v4.1 “FRAME”.

This release focuses on refining the image, character and subtitle layout on each individual slide. You can enlarge a diagram on one page, move a character away from important content, or hide subtitles on the final slide without changing the rest of the project.

sections.title: Change the image size and position on just one slide
sections.intro: Set image scale, horizontal position and vertical position separately for each slide.

blocks.html:
If a portrait image appears among landscape slides, you can make only that image smaller and centre it. The same controls help you enlarge a diagram or leave room for subtitles.

Select the slide in Normal mode, open the Slide Settings tab, then turn on the per-slide adjustment. Use the sliders or drag directly in the preview.

blocks.alt: Per-slide adjustment enabled for a still slide image
blocks.caption: Drag the image in the preview to move it, or use its corner handles to resize it

items: Switch the override on and off to compare it with the global setting; entered values remain when it is off
Reset any single value to the global setting
Available for video slides using the standard layout
Per-slide adjustment is not used when a video fills the screen

blocks.title: 💡 A stable view while adjusting
blocks.text: Image animation is temporarily removed while you adjust the layout, so the base position stays visible.

sections.title: Refine characters, subtitles and speech bubbles slide by slide
sections.intro: Choose a speaking character on the slide and change only that character’s presentation.

blocks.html: The new Character & Subtitles tab controls character icon size and position, subtitle or speech-bubble text size and position, and visibility. The character’s main settings and other slides remain unchanged.

blocks.alt: Adjusting a character and speech bubble in the Character and Subtitles tab
blocks.caption: Drag character icons, subtitles and speech bubbles directly in the preview

items: Move a character away from a chart
Reduce speech-bubble text on a slide with a long explanation
Hide only the character icon when a photograph needs more room
Hide subtitles while keeping narration
Match speech-bubble height to the amount of text

blocks.title: 🔊 Audio and duration do not change
blocks.text: Hide affects only visibility; audio and slide duration stay the same. Horizontal subtitle positioning is available for speech-bubble characters.

sections.title: Copy a layout to other characters or slides
sections.intro: Apply a useful adjustment to selected destinations instead of repeating it slide by slide.

blocks.html: Copy This Adjustment can apply the settings to another character on the same slide, or to the same character on selected slides. Nothing changes until you select the destinations and confirm the application.

blocks.alt: Dialog for copying character and subtitle adjustments to other slides
blocks.caption: Slides that already have individual adjustments are marked in the list

blocks.title: ⚠️ Existing individual adjustments are overwritten
blocks.text: One Undo reverses the whole operation. The copied values are offsets and scale relative to global settings, so characters with different base sizes or positions may not look identical.

blocks.title: 🎞️ Preview and still-document export
blocks.text: The editor preview updates less frequently, so also check motion in full playback. Still-image and PDF exports place the sticker at its base position without active motion.

sections.title: Combine fonts by language
sections.intro: Choose one font in each of four tabs: Japanese, Latin, Chinese and Korean.

blocks.alt: Choosing a Latin font from several style groups
blocks.caption: For example, pair a readable Japanese sans-serif with a display face for Latin headings

blocks.html:
This is useful for mixed Japanese and English documents, language-learning materials and multilingual subtitles. It changes the appearance of text; it does not translate it.

The preview is redrawn after fonts load, and export now waits for the required fonts.

blocks.title: 🌐 Downloading additional fonts
blocks.text: An internet connection is required to load additional fonts.

sections.title: Choose what to include in a lighter backup
sections.intro: Include only the characters used by the project, or leave out the video files themselves.

blocks.alt: Choosing characters and videos for a backup and checking its estimated size
blocks.caption: Review included items and the estimated backup size before saving

blocks.html: If Include Videos is off, editing information such as video-slide duration, thumbnails, audio, subtitles and stickers remains in the backup. When the original video is stored separately, this produces a lighter editing-data backup.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Keep excluded media separately
blocks.text: A backup without videos cannot play the originals in another environment. Select the original files again after restoring. Include the characters you use when moving to another computer.

blocks.text: The source video’s smoothness is retained with either export setting. This does not interpolate motion that was not present in the source.

sections.title: How to update to v4.1
sections.intro: Existing customers can copy v4.1 from the same shared link in the paid note article.

blocks.title: 💾 Make a backup first
blocks.text: If you want to carry over projects, libraries and settings, create a backup from Save Data before updating.

blocks.html: To update the Apps Script edition while keeping the same URL, replace the existing Untitled.html and AppBundle.html with the v4.1 versions, then redeploy the existing deployment as a new version.

For the local HTML edition, download and open the v4.1 local HTML file. Data from the previous browser or Apps Script project does not appear automatically in a new environment, so restore it from a backup.

sections.title: Make every slide clearer.
sections.intro: Arrange the image, characters and subtitles to suit the content of each page.

blocks.html:
v4.0 let you decide what to add above a slide and when it should appear. v4.1 “FRAME” lets you refine where the image, characters and subtitles sit — and how large they should be — while looking at that individual slide.

The workflow from preparing material and a script in Bundle Builder to finishing each slide in SlideCast Studio is now easier to control.
